From: Elena Rossi <elena@medica.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Andre Souza <andre.souza@healthsco.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on model-improvement exclusion & subprocessor access

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare our legal review I have a couple of points we need clarified on the DPA and operational evidence related to model improvement exclusions and prompt/response ownership: 

- Can Redwood commit to an explicit operational "no-model-improvement" carveout for our tenant data (no training, fine-tuning, or persistent model updates using HealthSCO prompts/responses)? We understand implementation varies; a short description of the controls would help.
- Please confirm whether any of our data (prompts/responses, logs, or derived telemetry) will transit or be accessible by subprocessors outside the EU. If so, which subprocessors and which countries?
- For procurement we need an evidence pack: subprocessor inventory, an architecture diagram showing where ephemeral caches/kv stores live, and a sample audit log demonstrating exports/egress events.
- Finally, we will want clarity on prompt/response IP—does Redwood assert any derivative rights, and can we get a short attestable statement for the contract?

Could you send a DPA redline + the inventory and an ETA for the evidence items? If easier, a 30-minute follow-up call with legal/ops next week would be great.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Legal & Privacy, Medica Group

Attachments: HealthSCO-questions.docx (referenced)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@medica.com>
Cc: Andre Souza <andre.souza@healthsco.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on model-improvement exclusion & subprocessor access

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Short answer first, then immediate next steps:

- Operational no-training: yes — we can commit to a tenant-scoped operational exclusion ("no model improvement") implemented via configuration and runtime isolation. That means HealthSCO traffic will not be used for any model parameter updates or persistent fine-tuning. We enforce this using separate serving pools and a toggle that disables telemetry ingestion into our model-improvement pipeline.

- Residency and subprocessors: the current subprocessor inventory is attached (subprocessor_inventory_202608.csv). Most subprocessors handling inference routing are in the EU; we do have a small set of monitoring/logging subprocessors in the US for hosted tiers — we will flag those and propose an onshore-only route for your tenant if needed.

- Evidence pack: attaching a DPA redline (DPA_Draft_v3.pdf) and an initial evidence checklist. Jordan, David — can you confirm the following for HealthSCO by EOD Friday?
  * A: Confirm which subprocessors handle logs vs. inference and whether any backups cross borders.
  * B: Provide a sanitized sample of an export/audit log (redacted) showing egress events.
  * C: Ops to confirm ephemerality of KV caches and whether any cached artifacts are persisted beyond session lifetime.

- Prompt/response IP: Redwood does not claim ownership of customer prompts or customer-provided responses. We can provide a short attestation clause for the DPA; legal to produce.

If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute call Monday to walk through the DPA and evidence pack.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_Draft_v3.pdf; subprocessor_inventory_202608.csv; evidence-checklist.md

- The attestation language you mentioned sounds good; please include explicit wording about no-training "at the tenant-level" (we're sensitive to any accidental leak into model-improvement pipelines).
- For onshore KMS: we prefer the onshore KMS route for keys used to encrypt our tenant artifacts. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports a dedicated onshore KMS key per tenant (or a bring-your-own-key flow)?
- Please include the sanitized audit log and the one-page KV/cache description in the pack. That will let our privacy team close the loop.

We're happy to do a 30-minute call — Monday morning CET would work. Also please send a DocuSign packet once legal prepares their final edits.
